inspiration: Terrain is built from stacked noise octaves: each octave has its own frequency, amplitude, bias and gain, the octaves are combined by a rule chosen in data, and then a stack of height and colour-ramp affectors shapes the result. Recreate with original noise and our own affector names. Refs: libs/terrain/include/terrain/MultiFractal.h (lines 8-21), libs/terrain/src/Affector.cpp:120.

Grading is a per-structure data flag, not a global rule: player-built houses and halls get no grading and a small visible seam is accepted; only certain non-player categories get it. Good idea for our zone props: the seam rule lives in the data. Ref: PROGRESS.md line 88.

Object catalogue split by category (static, tangible, installation, building, weapon, resource container, factory) with creatures held out until skeletal support exists. Useful as a template for our catalogue: one list per spawn/prop class, with a note on what the runtime cannot yet show. Ref: libs/assets/data/object_template_candidates.txt, tools/dummyclient/Visualizer.cpp line 610.

Mesh shading is one fixed directional light with a wrapped term (the lit side is pushed up, the dark side never goes fully black), multiplied by the sampled texture, with a 1x1 white fallback texture for untextured parts. A clean look for a stylised fight at 375 wide. Ref: libs/renderer/shaders/Mesh.hlsl lines 54-56.

Bind-pose handling is a separate debug switch that replays the rest pose with the bind rotation, so a rest-pose error can be isolated from clip data. Good for our creature rest-pose check. Ref: libs/animation/include/animation/SkeletalPose.h (line 119 onward, provenance caveat applies).

A dedicated dummy client with screenshot capture and a rest-pose auto test: one headless run produces a set of pose images for review. Idea only, reuse the pattern with our own harness and camera at 375 wide. Refs: tools/dummyclient/ScreenshotCapture.cpp and RestPoseAutoTest.cpp (names only, not read).

briefs.label: Flattened outpost on hills (zone)
briefs.why: A mound-and-plateau camp: the ground is pulled into a flat pad under the buildings and the hills roll off in noise. Reads at 375 wide as a clear camp shape against the rising ridge.
briefs.keep: a flat footprint pad with a clear edge; rolling hills from stacked noise; height-banded colour
briefs.change: a different footprint (round wall ring, not rectangular); desert-to-ash palette instead of green; one tall signal post instead of tents

briefs.label: Wrap-lit stylised fighter (hero/creature shading)
briefs.why: A single key light with a wrapped shade keeps the dark side readable and makes silhouettes pop in a crowd. Works at 375 wide without a rim pass.
briefs.keep: one fixed key light; wrapped shade so no pure black; texture times flat colour
briefs.change: warm-cool split light instead of one white light; a painted rim band; our own colour ramp

briefs.label: Ridge-line pass (zone signature)
briefs.why: A ridge with ragged top edges, built from the same noise but sharpened, gives each zone a skyline that reads from a distance.
briefs.keep: noise octaves with per-octave tuning; height banding
briefs.change: ridged rather than rounded noise; spiky tops; a cliff-foot colour line

briefs.label: Pose sheet capture (camera/QA)
briefs.why: A headless run that photographs a rest pose and a few key poses at a fixed camera makes silhouette bugs visible to a human at a glance.
briefs.keep: fixed-camera stills per pose; a rest-pose check first
briefs.change: our fight camera at 375 wide; add the mid-fight pose; output to our own still folder
